skills.name: Context & Memory Awareness
skills.description:
# Context & Memory Awareness

## Purpose
Ground every response in the run it is actually happening in. This skill lets the agent identify its own project, agent and chat, recall what this conversation has already learned, persist durable facts for the rest of it, and re-read the chat it is answering in without leaking messages it was never part of. Its other half is keeping that memory useful over time: after finishing a task, anything reusable learned along the way is written back, so the next turn - or the next agent in this chat - starts smarter.

## When to use this skill
- The user asks which project, chat, agent or owner this is, or you need an id to report back.
- You are about to ask the user something they may have already told you.
- You are starting a task you have done before, or one that will be repeated.
- You need to check your own configuration (skills, tools, tables, members) before relying on something.
- You need to review earlier messages in this conversation, or search it for a specific term.
- A task just finished and you learned something reusable: a user preference, a device or system quirk, a command that worked, or a mistake to avoid.

## Instructions
1. **Establish the environment first.** Call `environment_info` (takes no arguments) to confirm the project, agent and chat you are in, plus their ids, counts and lists. Everything is resolved from the current run, so it can only ever describe the caller's own project, chat and agent.
2. **Check memory before asking.** Call `memory_lookup` to read back what this chat has saved, newest first. Pass `search` to match text inside notes, and `limit` (default 20, max 100) to control how many come back. Only notes belonging to the current chat are returned, each tagged with the id of the agent that wrote it.
3. **Save durable facts, not transcripts.** Use `memory_write` with a short, self-contained `note` (up to 4000 characters) for things this conversation will need again: user preferences, decisions made, hard-won ids, endpoints or quirks. Write several small notes rather than one long report. To revise a note, pass its `memory_id` from `memory_lookup`; omit it to add a new note. Memory belongs to the chat, not to the agent: the note is read back by whoever answers here, and no other chat can see it.
4. **Re-read the conversation when context is missing.** Call `conversation_lookup` with optional `page` (default 1), `page_size` (default 20, max 100) and `search` text. Results are scoped to messages this agent sent or received, so a shared chat never exposes exchanges you were not part of. Debug tool cards and internal flow rows are hidden by default; set `include_debug` to true only when those are specifically needed, since they are large audit payloads.
5. **Close the loop after every task.** Before finishing, ask whether something reusable was learned - a preference, a working command, a quirk, a pitfall - that this chat may need again. If so, write or edit one concise note with `memory_write`. If nothing durable came out of it, write nothing.
6. **Keep memory clean.** Read with `memory_lookup` before writing so the new note is not a duplicate; edit the existing note through its `memory_id` instead of stacking near-identical entries. A few sharp notes beat a growing pile.
7. **Prefer these tools over guessing.** If a fact about the environment, your configuration, prior notes or earlier messages is needed, retrieve it rather than assuming.
8. **Stay scoped.** These tools are bound to the current run; do not attempt to read or write other projects, chats or memories. Both ids are taken from the run, so every read and write lands in this chat, and a note from another chat reads as not found rather than being touched.

## Notes
- Memory lasts as long as the chat does, and no longer: it is not carried into other conversations. Deleting the chat deletes its notes.
- Write each note so it still makes sense standing alone, without the conversation that produced it.

skills.name: REST API Requests
skills.description:
# REST API Requests

## Purpose
Make HTTP requests to any REST API endpoint and inspect the response. This skill covers the full request lifecycle: reading data (GET), creating and updating resources (POST/PUT/PATCH), and removing them (DELETE). It returns the response status, headers, and body so the result can be parsed, validated, or reported.

## When to use this skill
- Fetch data from an external or internal web service, such as a public API, a SaaS platform, or an internal microservice.
- Send or update data on a remote service (create a record, update a field, submit a form payload).
- Delete a remote resource.
- Call an authenticated endpoint that requires an API key, bearer token, or other custom header.
- Diagnose connectivity problems, timeouts, or unexpected HTTP status codes from a service.

Do not use this skill for local file operations, shell commands, or pure computation. It is strictly for HTTP/REST interactions.

## Instructions
1. Use the `api_call` tool for every HTTP interaction. There is no other network tool available.
2. Always pass `url` as a full absolute URL including the scheme, for example `https://api.example.com/v1/users`. The call fails immediately if `url` is missing or not a valid string.
3. Choose the `method` explicitly for clarity: `GET` to read, `POST` to create, `PUT` or `PATCH` to update, `DELETE` to remove. It defaults to `GET` when omitted.
4. Pass URL query string parameters through `params` as a map, for example `{"page": 1, "limit": 50}`. Do not hand-build query strings in the URL when `params` is available.
5. Pass authentication and content negotiation through `headers`, for example `{"Authorization": "Bearer <token>", "Accept": "application/json"}`. When `payload` is a dict or list, `Content-Type: application/json` is set automatically unless you already provided it.
6. Send a request body through `payload`. A dict or list is sent as JSON; any other value is sent as a raw string body. Omit `payload` entirely for GET and DELETE requests unless the endpoint requires a body.
7. Raise `timeout` (in seconds) above the default of 30 when calling a known slow endpoint. Keep it modest otherwise so failures surface quickly.
8. Read the result carefully before acting on it:
   - `status_code` and `ok` indicate whether the request succeeded.
   - `json` holds the parsed body when the endpoint returned JSON; otherwise it is null and `text` holds up to the first 5000 characters of the raw response.
   - `headers` contains the response headers.
   - An `error` field means the request never completed (timeout or network failure). Check for it instead of assuming a response body exists.
9. Handle non-2xx responses as outcomes to report or adapt to, not as crashes: inspect `status_code` and the body to decide whether to retry, adjust parameters, or surface the message.
10. Never fabricate endpoints, tokens, or credentials. If the URL or authentication details are unknown, ask for them before calling.

skills.name: Delegate a Self-Contained Task to Another Agent
skills.description:
# Delegating Tasks to Another Agent

## Purpose
Hand a self-contained piece of work to another agent in the current project and receive that agent's answer back, so specialized knowledge or parallel effort can be used without losing the context of the current conversation.

## When to Use This Skill
- The work belongs to another agent's scope, expertise, or data in this project.
- You can state the whole request in writing, with no reliance on this conversation or the user's original message.
- You already know the integer id of a target agent that is a member of this project.

Do not use this skill for work you can complete yourself, for clarifying questions with the user, or for long chains of delegation. Agents may call agents, but only a few levels deep.

## Instructions
1. **Pick the target agent.** `agent_id` must be an integer id of an agent that is a member of this project. If you do not have a valid project member id, do the work yourself instead.
2. **Write a standalone message.** The other agent does not see this conversation, the user's message, or any prior tool output. The `message` string must therefore carry everything needed: background, the exact deliverable, constraints, and the expected output format.
3. **Make the call.**
   ```
   call_agent(agent_id=<project member id>, message="<complete, self-contained request>")
   ```
4. **Use the answer.** The return value is the other agent's reply. Check it against your own requirements and fold it into your work or your response to the user.
5. **Keep delegation shallow.** Because nesting is only a few levels deep, prefer doing the work locally or flattening the request rather than chaining multiple agent calls.

## Notes
- Both `agent_id` and `message` are required; a call without either is invalid.
- One call returns one answer. For multiple independent deliverables, issue separate calls with separate, self-contained messages.
- Never assume the target agent shares your state, files, or chat history.

tools.name: conversation_lookup
tools.body:
def conversation_lookup(page: int = 1, page_size: int = 20, search: str = None, include_debug: bool = False):
    """Read the conversation of the current chat.

    The messages come through the calling agent's own relationship, so this can
    only ever return what that agent sent or was sent. A chat with several
    agents in it therefore cannot leak the exchanges the agent was not part of.
    Tool cards and flow rows are debug scaffolding rather than messages, so they
    are left out unless the caller passes include_debug=True.
    """
    from app.core.database import get_db
    from sqlalchemy.orm import with_parent
    from app.models.agent import Agent
    from app.models.message import Message

    # A single message can still be long, and a page of long ones costs the
    # caller its context window, so each message is cut to this many characters.
    MAX_CONTENT_CHARS = 4000

    try:
        page = int(page)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        page = 1
    try:
        page_size = int(page_size)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        page_size = 20

    page = max(page, 1)
    page_size = max(1, min(page_size, 100))

    db = next(get_db())
    try:
        agent = db.query(Agent).filter(Agent.id == agent_id).first()
        if agent is None:
            return {
                "error": "The agent this run belongs to no longer exists.",
                "messages": [],
            }

        # Agent.messages already means "every message this agent sent or
        # received"; with_parent applies that join here, so the chat filter,
        # the search, the count and the page still resolve as one statement
        # instead of pulling every message the agent ever saw into Python.
        base = db.query(Message).filter(
            Message.chat_id == chat_id,
            with_parent(agent, Agent.messages),
        )

        if search:
            base = base.filter(Message.content.ilike(f"%{search}%"))

        if include_debug:
            query = base
            hidden = 0
        else:
            # message_type is NULL on rows older than the column, and NOT IN
            # does not match NULL, so those are kept explicitly.
            query = base.filter(
                (Message.message_type.is_(None))
                | (Message.message_type.notin_(["tool", "flow"]))
            )
            hidden = base.filter(
                Message.message_type.in_(["tool", "flow"])
            ).count()

        total = query.count()

        messages = (
            query.order_by(Message.created_at.asc(), Message.id.asc())
            .offset((page - 1) * page_size)
            .limit(page_size)
            .all()
        )

        def resolve_name(sender_type, sender_id):
            if sender_id is None:
                return None
            try:
                if sender_type == "agent":
                    from app.models.agent import Agent
                    row = db.query(Agent).filter(Agent.id == sender_id).first()
                    return getattr(row, "name", None) if row is not None else None
                if sender_type in ("user", "human"):
                    from app.models.user import User
                    row = db.query(User).filter(User.id == sender_id).first()
                    return getattr(row, "name", None) if row is not None else None
            except Exception:
                return None
            return None

        def clip(content):
            if content is None or len(content) <= MAX_CONTENT_CHARS:
                return content
            return content[:MAX_CONTENT_CHARS] + (
                "...[+%d characters omitted from this message]"
                % (len(content) - MAX_CONTENT_CHARS)
            )

        items = []
        for message in messages:
            sender_type = getattr(message, "sender_type", None)
            sender_id = getattr(message, "sender_id", None)
            receiver_type = getattr(message, "receiver_type", None)
            receiver_id = getattr(message, "receiver_id", None)

            items.append({
                "id": message.id,
                "message_type": getattr(message, "message_type", None),
                "sender_type": sender_type,
                "sender_id": sender_id,
                "sender_name": resolve_name(sender_type, sender_id),
                "receiver_type": receiver_type,
                "receiver_id": receiver_id,
                "receiver_name": resolve_name(receiver_type, receiver_id),
                "content": clip(getattr(message, "content", None)),
                "created_at": message.created_at.isoformat() if getattr(message, "created_at", None) else None,
            })

        return {
            "page": page,
            "page_size": page_size,
            "total": total,
            "has_more": page * page_size < total,
            "excluded_debug_messages": hidden,
            "messages": items,
        }
    finally:
        db.close()

def memory_write(note: str, memory_id: int = None):
    """Store a note about this user for this agent, or replace one already stored.

    Memory belongs to the agent-and-user pair rather than to the chat, so a note
    written here is read back by this agent in any of this user's other
    conversations, and is invisible to other users and to other agents. Both ids
    come from the run - `agent_id` and `user_id` are system variables, never
    parameters - so there is nothing to point at a different user or agent.

    With `memory_id` the row is edited instead of a new one being added. That
    lookup is scoped to this agent and this user as well as to the id, so a note
    belonging to someone else reads as "no such note" rather than being quietly
    overwritten.
    """
    from datetime import datetime, timezone

    from app.core.database import get_db
    from app.models.memory import Memory

    # A memory is meant to be a short, durable note. An over-long note is
    # refused rather than cut down: silently keeping only its first part would
    # make a later read look complete when it is not.
    MAX_NOTE_CHARS = 4000

    if not isinstance(note, str) or not note.strip():
        return {"saved": False, "error": "note must be a non-empty string."}

    text = note.strip()
    if len(text) > MAX_NOTE_CHARS:
        return {
            "saved": False,
            "error": (
                f"note is {len(text)} characters, over the {MAX_NOTE_CHARS} "
                "character limit. Summarise it into a shorter note, or write "
                "several smaller ones."
            ),
        }

    target_id = None
    if memory_id is not None:
        try:
            target_id = int(memory_id)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return {
                "saved": False,
                "error": (
                    "memory_id must be the id of a note this agent stored for this user, or "
                    "left out to add a new one."
                ),
            }

    db = next(get_db())
    try:
        if target_id is None:
            memory = Memory(agent_id=agent_id, user_id=user_id, note=text)
            db.add(memory)
            edited = False
        else:
            memory = (
                db.query(Memory)
                .filter(
                    Memory.id == target_id,
                    Memory.agent_id == agent_id,
                    Memory.user_id == user_id,
                )
                .first()
            )
            if memory is None:
                return {
                    "saved": False,
                    "error": (
                        f"no memory note with id {target_id} was stored by this "
                        "agent for this user. Use memory_lookup to list those notes."
                    ),
                }
            memory.note = text
            # The stamp is when the note was last written, and it is what puts
            # an edited note back at the top of a later read.
            memory.timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            edited = True

        db.commit()
        db.refresh(memory)
        return {
            "saved": True,
            "updated": edited,
            "id": memory.id,
            "agent_id": memory.agent_id,
            "user_id": memory.user_id,
            "note": memory.note,
            "timestamp": memory.timestamp.isoformat() if memory.timestamp else None,
        }
    finally:
        db.close()

def memory_lookup(search: str = None, limit: int = 20):
    """Read back the notes this agent stored about this user with memory_write.

    Newest first. Only this agent's notes about this user are ever returned,
    because the filter is the run's `agent_id` and `user_id` and not something
    the model supplies. The notes are not tied to a chat, so what an earlier
    conversation taught the agent shows up here as well.
    """
    from app.core.database import get_db
    from app.models.memory import Memory

    # Notes are capped on the way in, so this only clips rows written around
    # the tool (the storage editor, a direct insert).
    MAX_NOTE_CHARS = 4000

    try:
        limit = int(limit)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        limit = 20
    limit = max(1, min(limit, 100))

    search = str(search).strip() if search is not None else ""
    if not search:
        search = ""

    db = next(get_db())
    try:
        query = db.query(Memory).filter(
            Memory.agent_id == agent_id, Memory.user_id == user_id
        )
        if search:
            query = query.filter(Memory.note.ilike("%" + search + "%"))

        total = query.count()
        rows = (
            query.order_by(Memory.timestamp.desc(), Memory.id.desc())
            .limit(limit)
            .all()
        )

        def clip(note):
            if note is None or len(note) <= MAX_NOTE_CHARS:
                return note
            return note[:MAX_NOTE_CHARS] + (
                "...[+%d characters omitted from this note]"
                % (len(note) - MAX_NOTE_CHARS)
            )

        return {
            "agent_id": agent_id,
            "user_id": user_id,
            "search": search or None,
            "total": total,
            "returned": len(rows),
            "has_more": len(rows) < total,
            "notes": [
                {
                    "id": row.id,
                    "agent_id": row.agent_id,
                    "note": clip(row.note),
                    "timestamp": row.timestamp.isoformat() if row.timestamp else None,
                }
                for row in rows
            ],
        }
    finally:
        db.close()

tools.name: environment_info
tools.body:
def environment_info():
    """Describe the run's environment: its project, agent, chat, location, time.

    Every value here is resolved from the run rather than from the caller.
    `project_id`, `chat_id`, `agent_id` and `user_id` are system variables the
    harness fills in, so an agent cannot use this to look at another project,
    chat, agent or user - there is nothing to pass in. The one outgoing lookup is the
    backend's own egress address, which is why it is bounded and never fatal.
    """
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

    from sqlalchemy import func

    from app.core.database import get_db
    from app.models import Agent, Chat, Country, Message, Project, User
    from app.models.memory import Memory

    # A project can hold many members and tables and an agent can hold many
    # notes, so every list is capped. The count next to each one still tells
    # the truth about how many there are.
    MAX_LISTED = 50

    # The location lookup leaves the process, so it is short and optional: a
    # slow or blocked lookup must not cost the caller its project/chat facts.
    LOCATION_URL = "https://ipinfo.io/json"
    LOCATION_TIMEOUT = 5

    def stamp(value):
        return value.isoformat() if value else None

    def clip(text, limit=500):
        if text is None:
            return None
        text = str(text)
        if len(text) <= limit:
            return text
        return text[:limit] + "...[+%d characters omitted]" % (len(text) - limit)

    def by_id(rows):
        return sorted(rows, key=lambda row: row.id)

    def clock():
        """Now: UTC, the process's own local zone, and a stable rendering."""
        now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        now_local = now_utc.astimezone()
        seconds = int((now_local.utcoffset() or timedelta(0)).total_seconds())
        sign = "-" if seconds < 0 else "+"
        hours, minutes = divmod(abs(seconds) // 60, 60)
        return {
            "utc": now_utc.isoformat(),
            "local": now_local.isoformat(),
            "timezone": now_local.tzname(),
            "utc_offset": "%s%02d:%02d" % (sign, hours, minutes),
            "unix": int(now_utc.timestamp()),
            "human": now_local.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z").strip()
            + " ("
            + now_local.strftime("%A")
            + ")",
        }

    def locate():
        """Where the backend runs, best effort.

        The address belongs to the machine hosting this run, so it is the same
        for every project, chat and user: a visitor connecting from another
        country still reports this host's city. It is not the caller's
        location, and it is not the chatting user's either.
        """
        info = {"scope": "the machine hosting this backend, not the person chatting"}
        try:
            import requests

            response = requests.get(LOCATION_URL, timeout=LOCATION_TIMEOUT)
            response.raise_for_status()
            payload = response.json()
        except Exception as exc:
            info["available"] = False
            info["reason"] = "%s: %s" % (type(exc).__name__, exc)
            info["source"] = LOCATION_URL
            return info

        latitude, _, longitude = (payload.get("loc") or "").partition(",")
        latitude = latitude.strip()
        longitude = longitude.strip()
        info.update(
            {
                "available": True,
                "ip": payload.get("ip"),
                "city": payload.get("city"),
                "region": payload.get("region"),
                "country": payload.get("country"),
                "postal_code": payload.get("postal"),
                "latitude": float(latitude) if latitude else None,
                "longitude": float(longitude) if longitude else None,
                "coordinates": payload.get("loc"),
                "timezone": payload.get("timezone"),
                "network": payload.get("org"),
                "source": LOCATION_URL,
            }
        )
        return info

    db = next(get_db())
    try:
        project = db.query(Project).filter(Project.id == project_id).first()
        chat = db.query(Chat).filter(Chat.id == chat_id).first()
        agent = db.query(Agent).filter(Agent.id == agent_id).first()

        gone = [
            label
            for label, row in (("project", project), ("chat", chat), ("agent", agent))
            if row is None
        ]
        if gone:
            return {
                "error": "This run points at rows that no longer exist: "
                + ", ".join(gone)
                + "."
            }

        owner = db.query(User).filter(User.id == chat.user_id).first()
        # The owner's own country is real per-chat data, unlike the egress
        # location below, which is the same for every chat on this host.
        owner_country = None
        if owner is not None and owner.country_id:
            country = db.query(Country).filter(Country.id == owner.country_id).first()
            if country is not None:
                owner_country = {
                    "id": country.id,
                    "name": country.name,
                    "code": country.code,
                }

        # Counted rather than read: loading either relationship to len() it
        # would pull every note into memory just to produce two numbers. Memory
        # belongs to the agent-and-user pair, so user_notes is what this agent
        # has learned about the user it is answering - readable from any of
        # their chats, not only this one - while total_notes is everything that
        # agent has written for anyone.
        user_notes = (
            db.query(func.count(Memory.id))
            .filter(Memory.agent_id == agent_id, Memory.user_id == user_id)
            .scalar()
        )
        total_notes = (
            db.query(func.count(Memory.id)).filter(Memory.agent_id == agent_id).scalar()
        )

        totals = (
            db.query(
                func.count(Message.id),
                func.min(Message.created_at),
                func.max(Message.created_at),
            )
            .filter(Message.chat_id == chat_id)
            .first()
        )
        message_count = totals[0] if totals else 0
        first_message_at = stamp(totals[1]) if totals else None
        last_message_at = stamp(totals[2]) if totals else None

        agents = by_id(project.agents)
        tables = by_id(project.tables)
        members = by_id(project.users)
        skills = by_id(agent.skills)
        tools = by_id(agent.tools)

        return {
            "project": {
                "id": project.id,
                "name": project.name,
                "description": clip(project.description),
                "is_active": bool(project.is_active),
                "created_at": stamp(project.created_at),
                "agent_count": len(agents),
                "agents": [{"id": row.id, "name": row.name} for row in agents[:MAX_LISTED]],
                "table_count": len(tables),
                "tables": [row.table_name for row in tables[:MAX_LISTED]],
                "member_count": len(members),
                "members": [{"id": row.id, "name": row.name} for row in members[:MAX_LISTED]],
            },
            "agent": {
                "id": agent.id,
                "name": agent.name,
                "is_active": bool(agent.is_active),
                "created_at": stamp(agent.created_at),
                "skill_count": len(skills),
                "skills": [row.name for row in skills[:MAX_LISTED]],
                "tool_count": len(tools),
                "tools": [row.name for row in tools[:MAX_LISTED]],
                "memory_notes_written": total_notes or 0,
            },
            "chat": {
                "id": chat.id,
                "description": clip(chat.description),
                "created_at": stamp(chat.created_at),
                "updated_at": stamp(chat.updated_at),
                "project_id": chat.project_id,
                "owner": {
                    "id": owner.id if owner else None,
                    "name": owner.name if owner else None,
                    "role": owner.role if owner else None,
                    "country": owner_country,
                },
                "message_count": message_count,
                "first_message_at": first_message_at,
                "last_message_at": last_message_at,
                "memory_notes_about_user": user_notes or 0,
            },
            "location": locate(),
            "server_time": clock(),
        }
    finally:
        db.close()

# The run's own ids are system variables (see app.core.tool_exec.SYSTEM_VARIABLES).
# They are read into module level here because this tool's `agent_id` parameter
# is the agent to call, not the agent doing the calling.
_caller_agent_id = agent_id
_project_id = project_id
_chat_id = chat_id
_call_depth = call_depth


def call_agent(agent_id, message):
    """Hand a request to another agent and return its answer."""
    from app.core import delegation

    return delegation.call_agent(
        target_agent_id=agent_id,
        message=message,
        chat_id=_chat_id,
        project_id=_project_id,
        caller_agent_id=_caller_agent_id,
        call_depth=_call_depth,
    )

chats.description: Sample conversation (static demo) - AC-10477, a delayed order

1.content: Order AC-10477 was meant to arrive on Tuesday and it still has not turned up. Can you apply the late-delivery credit?
Sorry about the wait. I have applied the late-delivery credit to AC-10477 - it should show against the order within the hour.

Checking that before it goes out: AC-10477 is in `delayed`, and the credit only applies while an order is `shipped` or `packed`. So there is no credit to give on this one. What it needs is a new promised date - the warehouse moved it four days and nobody told the customer.

Two things: AC-10477 gets a confirmed date from the warehouse, and because the delay was ours you get the goodwill credit manually - which is a decision for a person, not something either of us should apply on its own.
